To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mechanotransduction requires the actin-based motility of the hair bundle and is mediated by mechanosensitive ion channels in the tips of stereocilia.
The hair bundle is a complex mechanotransduction machine that is capable of amplifying and transducing sound energy into neural impulses.

1) the hair-cell bundle is a mechanotransducer, 2) the bundle is composed of stereocilia that are connected to the plasma membrane via tip links, 3) the bundle is a self-organizing structure, 4) the bundle is an actin cytoskeleton that is highly organized and is composed of a large number of actin-binding proteins (ABPs), 5) the actin cytoskeletalon is a highly dynamic structure,
In summary, our research is concerned with
how hair cells sense and respond to sound, and how defects in the molecular machinery that drives these processes lead to hearing and balance disorders.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate hair cell development and function.
the development and function, and the molecular basis, of the hair cell's mechanotransducer (MT) complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hair-cell mechanosensation is not a passive phenomenon but rather an active, highly regulated process.
the cell-biological mechanisms of mechanotrans-duction in hair cells have yet to be fully elucidated, but are likely to involve the coordinated action of multiple proteins and pathways.
the mechanosensitivity of stereocilia depends not on a single molecular complex, but on an ensemble of interacting proteins that are distributed throughout stereocilia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hair cells are not passive sensors but rather are actively driven by their stereocilia to produce a mechanosensory response.
mechanotransduction is not a simple process of force being applied to the tip-links and the opening of mechanotransducer (MT) channels.
mechanosensory transduction is not a passive process but is an actively regulated process, and that this regulation involves the actin cytoskeleton and the myosin motors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

hair-cell stereociliary tips are the primary sites of mechanotransducing activity and that the actin core of the stereocilium, rather than the tip link, is the primary site for the amplification of mechanotransduced signals.
the hair-cell bundle is an active structure that is continuously deforming, and this is the basis for mechanosensitivity.
the stereocilia are not the sensors for the sound wave, as previously believed.
